gap: No result ChatGPT got states the built-in preamp's line-out voltage. Audio-Technica rates the AT-LP70X at 252 mV (240 mV for the AT-LP120XUSB) at 1 kHz, 5 cm/sec. Fluance rates both the RT81 and the RT81+ at 140 mV (−17 dBV) with no test condition. That is about 5 dB less signal into the same powered speakers, from a preamp with about 4–5 dB less implied gain (32 dB and 31 dB, against A-T's stated 36 dB).
standout_why: I compared against valveandvinyl.com/crosley-alternatives and platterandplinth.com/turntables/best-with-preamp, both opened 2026-11-10. Valve & Vinyl gives A-T's '36 dB nominal gain' and the RT81's weighted and unweighted S/N. Its own gaps note says no product on the page states a line output in mV, and it gives no gain figure for the RT81. Platter & Plinth gives no output level for any of its six picks. It lists only the PS-LX3BT's relative gain steps (−4/0/+6 dB). Valve & Vinyl already covers the differences in S/N and wow-and-flutter weighting (A-weighted, DIN-B, WTD), so that is not new. fewbetter.com, ranked #1, now serves an unrelated product list with no turntables.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's pick of the AT-LP70X for a shopper who will plug straight into powered speakers. Its line out is about 1.8× the voltage of the RT81 and RT81+ (20·log10(252/140) ≈ 5.1 dB). All of them sit below the −10 dBV (316 mV) consumer line reference, and the Fluance pair sits furthest below it. The Fluance therefore needs more volume from the speakers or amp to play as loud. The RT81+'s stronger cartridge (4.0 mV against 3.5 mV) does not raise its stated line output, which stays at 140 mV. As a result, upgrading from the RT81 to the RT81+ gives no extra level at the LINE output, going by Fluance's own figures.

findings.label: Line output (built-in preamp ON)
findings.value: 252 mV nominal at 1 kHz, 5 cm/sec (≈ −12.0 dBV)
findings.source_title: Audio-Technica AT-LP70X Fully Automatic Belt-Drive Turntable (Black/Grey) – Music Redone
findings.note: This is a retailer page that reproduces A-T's spec block. audio-technica.com (en-us, en-ca, en-au, en-gb) returned HTTP 403 to every fetch. Conversion: 20·log10(0.252 V) = −11.97 dBV.

findings.label: Phono output and preamp gain
findings.value: 4.0 mV nominal at 1 kHz, 5 cm/sec; 36 dB nominal gain, RIAA equalized
findings.source_title: Audio-Technica AT-LP70X Fully Automatic Belt-Drive Turntable (Black/Grey) – Music Redone
findings.note: Check: 252/4.0 = 63×, and 20·log10(63) = 36.0 dB, which matches the stated gain. The page also lists wow and flutter <0.25% (WTD) and S/N >55 dB, with no weighting given for the S/N.

findings.label: Line output and phono output
findings.value: LINE 240 mV nominal at 1 kHz, 5 cm/sec (≈ −12.4 dBV); PHONO 4 mV; gain 36 dB nominal
findings.note: This is a retailer page that reproduces A-T's spec block, because A-T's own pages returned 403. Implied gain: 240/4 = 60×, which is 35.6 dB. The page also lists wow and flutter <0.2% (WTD) at 3 kHz (JIS) and S/N >50 dB with no weighting.

findings.label: Line output (built-in preamp ON)
findings.value: 140 mV (−17 dBV), no test frequency or velocity stated
findings.source_title: RT81 Hi-Fi Vinyl Turntable Record Player with Diamond Needle - Walnut | Fluance
findings.note: This is the maker's US page. Unlike A-T, Fluance gives no 1 kHz, 5 cm/sec condition, so the two figures are comparable only if Fluance used the usual reference. Against the AT-LP70X: 20·log10(252/140) = 5.1 dB lower.

findings.label: Phono output, implied preamp gain, price
findings.source_title: RT81 Hi-Fi Vinyl Turntable Record Player with Diamond Needle - Walnut | Fluance
findings.note: Gain is my arithmetic: 140/3.5 = 40×, and 20·log10(40) = 32.0 dB. Fluance publishes no gain figure. The page also gives S/N of 67 dB or higher (A-weighted, 20 kHz LPF) and 60 dB or higher (unweighted), wow and flutter 0.2% with no weighting, a 'Texas Instruments preamp IC', and 'all electronics bypassed' when an external preamp is used.

findings.label: Line output, phono output, price
findings.value: LINE 140 mV (−17 dBV); PHONO 4.0 mV (±3 dB); implied gain ≈ 30.9 dB; $349.99
findings.source_title: RT81+ Elite High Fidelity Vinyl Turntable | Fluance
findings.note: The phono output rises from 3.5 mV to 4.0 mV with the AT-VM95E cartridge, but the stated line output stays at 140 mV. Implied gain: 140/4.0 = 35×, which is 30.9 dB. So either the preamp gain differs, or the 140 mV is a fixed figure that was not re-rated for the new cartridge. Fluance does not say which.

findings.label: Reviewer remark on preamp output
findings.value: The reviewer did not measure output level. He 'would like to see a higher output from the phono preamplifier'
findings.source_title: Fluance RT81 Turntable, Cartridge, and Phono Preamplifier Review | Secrets of Home Theater and High Fidelity
findings.note: John E. Johnson, Jr., 15 June 2016. He measured low-frequency motor noise 25 dB below the signal and could not bench-measure wow and flutter. The review's spec table labels 140 mV as 'phono output', but Fluance labels it as the line output.
